TCUST promotes four major missions: Charity, Medical Care, Education, and Humanity. Can you elaborate more on this?In 1966, Dharma Master Cheng Yen established the Tzu Chi Foundation in Hualien, on the east coast of Taiwan. With the spirit of self-discipline, diligence, frugality, and perseverance, Tzu Chi set out to help the poor and relieve suffering. The foundation’s mission started with Charity and over time extended into Medicine, Education, and Humanistic Culture. Tzu Chi originated in the remote Hualien area and expanded to five continents with chapters and offices in 57 countries. Tzu Chi provides aid to over 98 nations. Its volunteers selflessly contribute through a mindset of gratitude, expressing their sincerest care and support to each and every individual in need. Tzu Chi Foundation’s “Four Major Missions” consist of Charity, Medicine, Education, and Humanity.1. Mission of Charity“Educating the rich to help the poor; inspiring the poor to realize their riches.”Tzu Chi pays attention not only to the effectiveness of its aid and assistance but also focuses on bringing out the good in everyone. By helping the poor, the rich get to feel the happiness of giving and find the true meaning of life. Likewise, the poor are motivated to harbor love abundantly and help out those less fortunate than themselves, so that they break away from perceived helplessness and despair. Consequently, more people become willing to help out others while enriching their spirits through contribution.2. Mission of Medicine“Patient-centered medical care that respects patients as teachers.”Among the four suffering states of life, illness is the most painful. During her charity visits, Dharma Master Cheng Yen realized that many families became poor after encountering some major illness. Therefore, she founded the Tzu Chi Free Clinic for the Poor in 1972, which began Tzu Chi’s mission of Medicine. In 1986, the Hualien Tzu Chi General Hospital opened, and its guiding principles were “respect life” and “patient-centered”. Tzu Chi Taiwan’s medical network was completed by the openings of additional hospitals in Yuli, Guanshan, Dalin, Taipei, and Taichung. The medical staff, supported by large teams of volunteers, aim to perfect the “Four Entireties” of patient care: the entire treatment process, the patient’s entire body, the patient’s entire family, and the entire medical team. The goal is to ensure proper care of the body, mind, and soul of the patient. From city to countryside, from the mountain to the sea, Tzu Chi’s comprehensive medical network provides the people of Taiwan with top quality medical service that consists of the latest technology and the warm human touch.3. text: 首頁原始資料集學生團隊獲選花蓮青年計畫補助系所原始資料集學生團隊獲選花蓮青年計畫補助系所原始資料，保留官方發布語言。以下資料保留官方發布原文；文件與外部連結亦維持原始語言。慈濟大學經營管理學系再傳佳績！ 由本系大二學生周禹嫻、林芷萱、高翊翔、吳進福及施柏言組成之團隊「嶼食織心」，在林信宏老師指導下，成功入選花蓮縣政府青年發展中心辦理之「2026花蓮青年鏈結地方產業專題成果補助計畫」，獲得新臺幣25,000元行動獎勵金支持。 「青年鏈結地方產業專題成果補助計畫」以花蓮縣大專校院青年為主要對象，鼓勵學生運用專業知能，結合地方產業需求，透過專題研究與實作參與地方發展，深化青年對在地議題的理解與投入，並培養未來投入地方創生與產業發展的人才。 本次入選團隊以「嶼食織心」為題，展現學生對花蓮地方產業、文化資源及永續發展議題的關注，並透過跨領域思考與實務規劃，提出具地方特色與創新價值的行動方案。此次獲得補助，不僅肯定團隊成員的努力與創意，更展現本系長期推動地方創生、產業鏈結及實作學習的成果。 經營管理學系持續鼓勵學生走入社區與產業現場，透過專題研究、實務參與及跨域合作，培養解決地方問題與創造社會價值的能力。期待「嶼食織心」團隊在後續計畫執行過程中持續深化成果，為花蓮地方產業發展注入更多青年創意與能量。 慈濟大學經營管理學系全體師生同賀！ https://ydc.org.tw/zh-hant/activity/news/form/410/閱讀原始公告
